purpose: Qualify tool-geometry-derived fixed-axis lathe removal envelopes upstream of the accepted RCS-010 axisymmetric material-domain provider.

sources.fact_used: A representative CNMG turning setup is shown with 95 degree entering angle and 0.8 mm insert nose radius; these values seed an abstract research tool, not a proprietary catalogue dependency.
Turning guidance treats entering angle and insert nose radius as geometry-critical parameters and notes that changing entering angle changes cutting-force direction.
Current parting/grooving inserts expose explicit cutting width and left/right corner radii, supporting a width-plus-corner-radius abstract groove/parting model.

hypotheses.statement: For a bounded fixed-axis subset, realistic circular-nose turning/boring geometry plus canonical tool-centre trajectories can derive a material envelope that agrees with an independent capsule oracle and remains suitable for the RCS-010 material domain.
Tool/holder approach geometry creates a real capability predicate: some undercut/reachability requests must hand off or refuse rather than be represented as an axisymmetric target profile.

A grooving/parting tool described by cutting width and corner radius can express both a one-body groove and a complete cut-through that produces two material bodies without silently discarding either body.

falsification: Independent envelope/material oracle disagreement exceeds the declared construction budget for a case claimed qualified.
The OCCT reconstruction/STEP comparator produces invalid topology, wrong body count, material deviation outside budget, or a hidden approximation that is reported as exact.
A reachability collision is ignored to keep an operation inside the specialized provider.
A complete parting case loses either disconnected material body.

policies.frame: right-handed z/r workpiece section; z is spindle axis and r is non-negative radial coordinate
policies.nose_model: Minkowski sweep of a circular insert nose along an explicit canonical tool-centre polyline
policies.generator_algorithm: independently polygonized capsule envelope with bounded circular chord error
policies.oracle_algorithm: closed-form vertical bounds of the exact segment-plus-disc capsule, integrated on a separately implemented high-resolution material oracle
policies.analytic_nose_surface_policy: The research polygon adapter is a bounded material/reconstruction probe, not qualification that an exact circular nose is preserved as a torus in STEP. Exact analytic nose-surface reconstruction remains separately visible in results rather than being silently claimed.
